fix_summary: ADR-0170 Phase C.3 — lazy ControllerRegistry init. Split _doInit (RVF storage) from _doInitRegistry (agentdb_* registry). memory_*-axis routes (routeMemoryOp, routeEmbeddingOp) call ensureRouter(); agentdb_*-axis routes (routePatternOp, routeFeedbackOp, routeSessionOp, routeLearningOp, routeReflexionOp, routeCausalOp, getController) call ensureRegistry(). The benchmark's memory store/search ops are memory_*-axis-only, so they no longer pay the agentdb_* substrate bootstrap cost per CLI invocation.

gate_decision.rule: no >10% regression vs SQLite baseline on any of (store p50, store p95, search p50, search p95, total wall). Speedup is fine.
gate_decision.notes: Per ADR-0170 §'Performance benchmark gate': the rule is about regressions (slowdowns) — 'if pglite is slower by >10% on any metric, root-cause fix the regression'. Speedup is acceptable. The 14-40% speedup is the direct result of the C.3 lazy init: the benchmark drives `memory store` + `memory search`, both memory_*-axis-only operations. Pre-C.3 they paid the full agentdb_* registry init cost on every CLI invocation; post-C.3 they only init RVF. The agentdb_* substrate is initialized on-demand by agentdb_*-axis tools (agentdb_reflexion_store, agentdb_skill_create, etc.) — those still pay the full init cost when invoked, which is correct behavior.
